column1: # Best-effort-after-commit guard exemption list — GUARD-1 session.
# internal/core/besteffort_guard_test.go (TestBestEffortGuard_UnprotectedPostWriteDiscard),
# server/http/handlers/besteffort_guard_test.go, and
# server/grpc/services/besteffort_guard_test.go each fail the build when a
# non-test function discards a call's result/error (`_ = f(...)`) that
# textually follows a storage-write call in the same function, and the
# discard is not routed through goSafe(...)/besteffort.Run(...) (package
# internal/besteffort). Every hit must either be migrated to besteffort.Run,
# or get a reviewed row here.
# Format: <package>:<function>\t<reason>
# <package> is the scanned root (internal/core, server/http/handlers,
# server/grpc/services) so identically-named functions in different packages
# don't collide. <function> matches the guard's own fn label: "Name" for a
# free function, "(*Type).Name" for a method.
# Seeded 2026-10-03 (GUARD-1): every row below is a caller-side discard of a
# callee that ALREADY recovers its own panic internally (the callee is its
# own choke point -- evictUserSessionCache, deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict,
# notifyBreakGlassAdmins, revokeProjectDynamicSecretLeases,
# seedProjectEnvironment, evictMachineIdentityCacheOrFlush, emitAudit) —
# this caller-side AST walk cannot see that the callee is already safe, so
# every one of its callers that discards the result shows up as a hit here.
# None of these are migrated to besteffort.Run at the call site because the
# callee's own protection is the correct layer (re-wrapping at every call
# site would duplicate the recover, and some of these callees have bespoke
# audit-on-panic/fail-closed-cache-flush logic besteffort.Run's generic
# recover would not reproduce — see each callee's own doc comment).
# The callee itself: account.go's evictUserSessionCache recovers its own
# panic and logs, called from several role-removal sites (rbac_management.go)
# with no return value to discard at all, so it produces no caller-side hit —
# listed for completeness of the "callee already protected" corpus.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).evictUserSessionCache
column2: callee recovers its own panic (account.go); no bespoke logic to lose, but re-wrapping at every call site would duplicate the recover for no benefit.

column1: # The callee itself: account.go's deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict recovers its
# own panic, sets a named return (err = nil) so the discard is literally
# correct either way, AND writes EventSessionRevocationPanicked under the
# affected user's ID on a panic — besteffort.Run's generic log would lose
# that per-user audit trail.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict
column2: callee recovers its own panic + audits under the affected user's ID (account.go); besteffort.Run's generic log would lose that audit trail.

column1: # Every caller-side discard of deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict above: the
# callee is already safe, so these are not independently vulnerable. Found by
# this guard's own AST walk, which cannot see protection inside a callee.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).ActivateMFA
column2: discards deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict, whose own recover already closes the gap (mfa.go).

column1: internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).DisableMFA
column2: discards deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict, whose own recover already closes the gap (mfa.go).

column1: internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).DeleteWebAuthnCredential
column2: discards deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict, whose own recover already closes the gap (webauthn.go).

column1: internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).FinishWebAuthnRegistration
column2: discards deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict, whose own recover already closes the gap (webauthn.go).

column1: internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).UpdateSCIMUser
column2: discards deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict, whose own recover already closes the gap (scim.go); the "write" this guard matched (Unlock@263) is a mutex unlock, not a storage write — a benign false match, left here rather than silently dropped.

column1: # break_glass.go's notifyBreakGlassAdmins: whole-function choke point with a
# named return (err = nil on panic) and its own EventBreakGlassNotifyPanicked
# audit write under the affected project's ID — same shape as
# deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict above.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).notifyBreakGlassAdmins
column2: callee recovers its own panic + audits under the affected project's ID (break_glass.go); besteffort.Run's generic log would lose that audit trail.

column1: # catalog.go's revokeProjectDynamicSecretLeases: whole-function choke point
# that writes dynamic_secret.project_cascade_failed on both the returned-error
# AND the panic path — a richer failure record than besteffort.Run's generic
# log, read by the lease-revocation sweep/manual-retry tooling.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).revokeProjectDynamicSecretLeases
column2: callee recovers its own panic + writes a structured cascade-failure audit event read by the lease sweep (catalog.go); besteffort.Run's generic log would lose that.

column1: # catalog.go's seedProjectEnvironment: runs inside the SAME outer transaction
# (storage.WithTransaction) that created the project row, via a nested
# SAVEPOINT -- its own doc comment explains why an audit write from inside
# here would self-deadlock SQLite's single writer (a different connection via
# c.storage while tx itself still holds an open write transaction). It also
# returns a structured *projectEnvSeedFailure, not a plain error, for the
# caller to audit AFTER the outer transaction commits. besteffort.Run doesn't
# fit this shape without reproducing all of that by hand.
internal/core:seedProjectEnvironment
column2: runs inside a nested SAVEPOINT with a documented deadlock-avoidance constraint and a structured non-error return value; not a besteffort.Run shape.

column1: # machine_identities.go's evictMachineIdentityCacheOrFlush: on panic, its
# recover does MORE than log -- it fails closed by flushing every
# machine-token cache entry system-wide (c.machineTokenCacheFlusher) when the
# exact credential hashes can't be determined. besteffort.Run's generic
# recover has no hook for that fail-closed fallback.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).evictMachineIdentityCacheOrFlush
column2: callee's recover triggers a fail-closed, system-wide cache flush fallback (machine_identities.go); besteffort.Run has no equivalent hook.

column1: # service.go's emitAudit: the single busiest choke point in the system —
# every c.Log*/writeAuditEvent* call funnels through it (confirmed by
# TestDirectLogAuditEventCallersAreSafe). Its recover already closes the
# panic gap, keeps its own specific "SECURITY: failed to persist audit
# event..." log wording (existing log-based alerting may key off it), and
# its returned-error branch already deliberately skips the auditForwarder/
# auditStream side effects on failure — re-deriving that exact control flow
# through besteffort.Run's generic wrapper is pure churn risk on the hottest
# path in the codebase for no behavioral gain.
internal/core:(*KeyorixCore).emitAudit
column2: callee already recovers + has its own specific SECURITY log wording on the hottest path in the system; migrating is pure churn risk for no gain.
